about: What changed on the productions pages, newest first: one entry per commit that touched site/productions, taken from the repository's history when the pages were last built. The site's current version and commit are in /version.json (the version is made by the deploy from the git tags). The commit that carries this file is not in it.

changes.what: Agile Cells v0.1: registered and built (eight scenes, 78.5 s, vertical)
changes.detail:

  one cell; a person and agents join; roles, rules and work bud out as files; it
  grows to 10, 20, 30, 50 roles as an org chart and folds onto a shelf.

Not yet seen by critics or test viewers; not for the owner yet.

changes.what: Session refresh document and article: the hand-over as a compaction we control
changes.detail:
From Dinis Cruz's words of 28 Nov 2026, given as his account and not as a measurement: Claude's own compaction is
not controlled; a hand-over is one done on purpose. What the Markdown note holds (history, state, next tasks,
kept by a librarian, aiming at zero context loss); what the new session loads (rules, the agent behaviour
policies from RiskMandate, role, state); learnings that become skills. Reviews by the conductor and the maestro
are asked for.

changes.what: Each production as a small website; reviews, script, team and article pages; How we refresh a session v0.4
changes.detail:
From Dinis Cruz's second feedback, 28 Nov 2026:
- A menu on every page of a production (overview, watch, storyboard, reviews, script, article, team and its
  own pages), so a reviewer can move around one film without going back.
- Reviews page: the owner's feedback, five synthetic test viewers of v0.3 (outside models through OpenRouter,
  shown stills and the narration), the two critics of v0.1, and the signed reviews.
- Script page: the film as a screenplay. Team page: who did what, on which model. Article: a companion piece
  with frames of the film, the real one line that starts a new session, and what the refresh did not save.
- v0.4: a line of context on every scene (the problem, why, our rule, steps 1 to 3, the result, copy this),
  the three steps in the voice, and the team that made it as the last scene. The voice no longer says it is
  made by AI; the label on every frame does. About 90 seconds. The pictures are v0.3's.
- Storyboard cards: a Stop the film button and a mark on the microphone button while it listens.
- productions.json: the next film asked for, how this one was made, as an agile cell.
- player.js changed, so digests changed; the self-check reviews are signed again.

changes.what: How we refresh a session v0.3: a cover that says what and why, a brand line on every scene; dictation that shows it is listening
changes.detail:
From Dinis Cruz's first feedback on the film, 28 Nov 2026:
- v0.3 opens with a cover: the title, and why (long sessions with Claude burn tokens; this is how we recycle
  ours). The nine scenes after it are v0.2's. About 85 seconds.
- The player draws a production's brand line at the top of every scene when scenes.json names one
  ('Sovereign Website · Productions' here; the wording waits for the owner's word). Other productions are unchanged.
- Speaking a comment on the review and storyboard pages now pauses the film, shows the words in the box as they
  are spoken and keeps them scrolled into view, with a line saying it is listening.
- player.js changed, so every version's digest changed; the self-check reviews are signed again.

changes.what: A new feedback lane and a new media vault for the successor session
changes.detail:
The first lane and the first media vault's write key ended with the first session at the hand-over of 28 Nov 2026.
- send/inbox.json: the new lane's vault, sealed to this session's public key. Tested: configure, two sealed
  writes, list, read. Every browser needs a new sign-in code; its own key is unchanged.
- media.json: a new vault with its published read key (a read-only clone with it was tested); the first vault
  stays listed as read only, with what it holds.

changes.what: Session refresh film: a first storyboard; the Agile film names its source site and family
changes.detail:
- session-refresh/storyboard/: nine beats, each with a sketch drawn from document.json's own numbers, its words,
  picture, motion and a 'so what'. About 75 seconds. The film is vertical (720 by 1280) from the start, at
  Dinis Cruz's word of 28 Nov 2026; the first sketches were drawn wide before that and fix content, not framing.
- The story of Agile: the production page and the first credits line now name the source, The history of Agile
  (agile.history.sovereignweb.site), and that it is part of the Sovereign Website family (sovereignwebsite.org),
  as Dinis asked on 28 Nov 2026. v0.3's digest changed with that one line.
- The self-check reviews are signed again with the successor session's key (same decisions and comments).

changes.what: c.productions: retire this session's key at the hand-over
changes.detail:
The successor session is up (28 Nov 2026, 02:39 UTC). A key can be published only in a commit that adds
site/keys/<name>.json alone, so this session moves its own key file to site/keys/retired/, marked
retired with its date and successor, which frees the name. Records signed with it (reviews, the lane's
grants) now point at the retired file and still verify. This is this session's last commit.

changes.what: For the successor: the lane's agent script, the scene-smith brief and how the loop is run
changes.detail:
Asked by the successor session. _build/lane_agent.py is the agent's side of the feedback lane (drain,
reply, grant); it holds no secret, only paths to files outside the repository. _build/scene-smith-brief.md
is the template every scene-smith got and the loop's steps, voice and frames included.

changes.what: c.productions: learnings for the successor, the things the restart note left out
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz wants losses of context at hand-overs found and the prompts fixed. What the first session
learnt the hard way: the checks and re-signing, testing limits, what this environment refuses, the
append lane's undocumented calls, what Dinis has asked for more than once, and who is where.

changes.detail:

cool, the savings that you get". session-refresh/production.json holds the brief, the so-what, the five

changes.what: Session refresh document: a measured hand-over, context before and after
changes.detail:

859,600 tokens to 118,600, the conversation part from 781,000 to 43,900, and a fixed floor of about
